units.title: 2c Core content of A Level Art and Design

outcomes.text: Engage in integrated critical, practical and theoretical study in art and design.
Work within relevant frameworks using a broad range of media, developing independence in exploring ideas and refining intentions.
Explain why understanding context helps explore ideas, feelings and meanings.
Show contextual understanding through critical evaluation in research, written analysis and practical work, including historical and contemporary practitioners, industries, cultures and events.
Show critical and contextual understanding throughout all processes and outcomes.
Show awareness of the roles, functions, audiences and consumers of art, craft and design.
Extend understanding of context through a related study of art theory, genre, subject matter, movement or historical framework.
Understand the importance of ongoing development and refinement and the links between practical and written material.
Identify and acknowledge all sources in a bibliography.
Know the broad range of media and approaches available, including traditional, digital and emerging technologies.
Reflect critically on art, craft and design to place own work in a framework of advanced study.
Show progression of ideas through sketchbooks, workbooks, journals, digital or audio presentations.
Take an applied approach, working to a brief and reflecting professional practice, constraints, audiences and clients.
Use drawing to record, communicate and visualise intentions, ideas and emotions, developing forms of drawing suited to the specialism.
Recognise drawing can take forms such as mark making, stitch, collage, storyboarding and 2D or 3D designs.
Record experiences and observations through drawing or other visual forms.
Research, gather, select and organise visual and other information.
Explore resources and analyse, discuss and evaluate images, objects and artefacts, making independent judgements.
Use knowledge of others' work to extend thinking and inform own work.
Generate and explore lines of enquiry with suitable media and techniques.
Make images and artefacts, review and modify work, and develop ideas in light of evaluations.
Organise and communicate ideas and solutions in visual, tactile or sensory forms.
Understand relevant materials, processes, technologies and resources.
Understand how ideas, feelings and meanings are conveyed and interpreted in images and artefacts.
Understand how images and artefacts relate to the time, place and social and cultural contexts in which they were made.
Understand continuity and change in genres, styles and traditions.
Use a working vocabulary and specialist terminology.

units.title: 2c Summary of specialisms and areas of study

outcomes.text: Name the seven specialisms: Combined, Fine Art, Graphic Communication, Photography, Textile Design, Three-Dimensional Design, and Critical and Contextual Studies.
Combined Specialisms: work in two or more specialisms, choosing areas of study within or across them.

units.title: 2c(i) Art, Craft and Design: Combined Specialisms (H600)
